subject: Launchpad revenue staircase, registration exceptions, and first-year rebate mechanics
messages:
From: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@launchpadsys.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: legal@launchpadsys.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launchpad x Redwood – pilot revenue mechanics + registration ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the engineering team was impressed with the latency and routing controls. Per our commercial call, I attached a first-pass term sheet with two commercial concepts we want to pilot: a tiered revenue "staircase" for the first 24 months and a short-window lead registration escape for strategic accounts.

High-level:
- Staircase: 30% rev share for months 0-6, 20% for 7-12, 10% after month 12 (volume thresholds in ANNEX A).
- Early adopter rebate: one-time rebate payable at EOY if Launchpad drives >$500k ARR in year 1.
- Registration exception: Launchpad requests a 60-day handback window for co-sourced enterprise deals where a technical proof-of-concept (PoC) is initiated by Launchpad.

I've attached the draft (LP-terms-draft.pdf) and the rebate matrix (ANNEX-A-rebate-matrix.xlsx). Legal flagged two items they'd like Redwood to confirm:
1) Escrow or holdback mechanism for the rebate fund (how do you guarantee funds if there's a churn/cancellation?)
2) Clawback and contract change handling if a customer converts to Redwood direct within the rebate window.

Would you and your RevOps/Partner ops folks be available for a quick 30-min sync tomorrow to align on registration gating and escrow mechanics?

Thanks,
Sarah O'Neill
Head of Strategic Alliances | Launchpad Systems
[attachment: LP-terms-draft.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)]
[attachment: ANNEX-A-rebate-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 28 KB)]

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@launchpadsys.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launchpad x Redwood – pilot revenue mechanics + registration ask

Thanks Sarah — and appreciate the attachments. Happy to run this down with the team. A few quick clarifying questions before the call so we can bring the right playbook: 

1) Registration exception scope — when you say "co-sourced enterprise deals where PoC is initiated by Launchpad" can you confirm minimal evidence items? Typical asks we need: signed SOW for PoC, named AE/SE owners, and a Launchpad-introduced lead record in HubSpot with date stamp. If Launchpad can supply those three, we can consider a limited exception.

2) Escrow mechanics — we generally don't hold third-party escrow for partner rebates. Two practical options we propose:
  - Holdback on Redwood invoices: Redwood withholds the rebate until EOY and pays out after verification; or
  - Partner-managed escrow: Launchpad maintains the escrow and we agree on audit rights and payout triggers.

3) Staircase timing — the ANNEX A's thresholds look fine, but we need to map "driven ARR" to how we attribute net-new vs. influenced deals (intro vs. inbound). Do you expect full attribution for any contact Launchpad touches, or only registered/intros with accepted MQLs?

I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Camila (partner ops), Ben (finance/revops), Marissa (legal ops), and Karthik (GTM). Proposed time: Mon 10am PT or Mon 2pm PT. Happy to take earlier if you prefer.

Next steps for us before the call: Camila will outline the registration workflow and typical evidence; Ben will draft suggested holdback wording; Marissa will flag legal redlines; Karthik will propose GTM milestones tied to staircase triggers.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Redwood internal note: attaching LP-terms-draft to calendar invite]

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launchpad x Redwood – pilot revenue mechanics + registration ask

Markus / Sarah — looping in quick operational detail so the call can be focused on exceptions and settlement.

Registration workflow we require for a successful "registered lead":
- Launchpad creates a lead record in HubSpot and assigns "source: Launchpad-intro";
- Launchpad provides a signed PoC SOW or email confirmation from customer that explicitly names Launchpad as primary implementer;
- Customer is not currently in a Redwood active contract for the same product SKU (to avoid double-counting).

If those three checks are present within 60 days of first contact, Redwood will accept registration and apply allocation for attribution. For the 60-day handback window Sarah proposed: we can accept it with these constraints:
- If Launchpad provides the three evidence items within the 60-day window, registration sticks;
- If the customer converts directly to Redwood without the evidence, Redwood reserves the right to decline registration and revert attribution.

On escrow/holdback: Ben — can you confirm the simplest legal/ops path? From an ops POV the holdback-on-invoice model is easiest (Redwood accrues the rebate liability on our books and pays out post-verification). Partner-managed escrow is more work for both sides (and creates reconciliation friction).

Action items for the call:
1) Ben to propose two short clauses (holdback and audit rights).
2) Marissa to mark any governance/legal traps in Annex A.
3) Karthik to align on the staircase milestones and how GTM activity influences thresholds.

I'll send a short pre-read that maps HubSpot fields + PoC evidence examples so Launchpad can prepare.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Sr. Partner Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@launchpadsys.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launchpad x Redwood – pilot revenue mechanics + registration ask

Sarah / Markus / team — following our sync I drafted two short options for the rebate/escrow paragraph and attached a redline version of LP-terms-draft.pdf. I also updated Annex A to reflect monthly recognition rather than lump-sum EOY payment (that helps reconcile churn during the year).

Option A (Redwood holdback):
- Redwood will accrue the partner rebate monthly as a receivable; payout happens at EOY after verification. If a registered customer churns before payout, prorated clawback applies to the rebate amount tied to months after termination.

Option B (Partner-managed escrow):
- Launchpad funds an escrow account equal to 30% of forecasted rebates for year 1. Escrow releases are triggered quarterly upon joint verification. Partner maintains right to audit. Clawback mechanics apply on customer churn.

Ops recommendation: go with Option A to keep reconciliation simple and avoid partner bank fees. Draft redline attached: [attachment: LP-terms-draft_REDLINE.pdf (PDF, 98 KB)].

Next steps:
- Sarah: confirm whether Launchpad can accept monthly accrual + EOY payout with prorated clawback, or if they need escrow for sales crediting reasons.
- Sarah: confirm whether the 60-day registration window is acceptable given the three-evidence rule Camila outlined.
- Marissa: please review my redlines for legal language and flag any unacceptable liability exposure.

If we get alignment on Option A and the registration evidence, I'll uplist the clause to the commercial template and we can roll this into a 90-day pilot SLA.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
